investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T20:51–20:58Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at this time. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Lower confidence — transient burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (e.g., from multiple eval runs or user activity) temporarily exhausted slots that would otherwise be available; slots may self-recover as existing VMs are cleaned up via the withCleanup wrapper visible at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T20:51–20:58Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at this time. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The agent pod remained unscheduled for ~142–148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote agent pod fails immediately with Unschedulable. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completes, no evidence is collected, and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie pods from prior eval runs may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are at capacity, making the effective schedulable pool size 0.

Tertiary — kata peer-pod infrastructure misconfiguration or node-level daemon failure: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource may not be correctly advertised by the node device plugin on the 2 eligible nodes, causing the reported capacity to be lower than actual hardware capacity.

Quaternary — eval cleanup not releasing VM resources: if a prior eval run's withCleanup handler (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) failed to delete agent pods, those pods may still be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, starving subsequent runs.
